summary.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.5% YoY to INR 2,545 crore, with hospital revenue up 19% to INR 2,187 crore and diagnostics gross revenue up 10.2% to INR 407 crore. Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP rose 15.8% to INR 568 crore, but margin eased to 22.3% from 22.6%, with hospitals at 21.5% versus 22.1%. Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: +15.8% YoY; margin vs 22.6% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before exceptional items

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,869 crore and 0.92x at 30 June 2025

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,187 crore (+19%) and operating EBITDA INR 471 crore at 21.5% margin versus 22.1%. Like-for-like margin excluding new Punjab, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR leased facilities was about 22%. Renal sciences grew 28%, neurosciences 27% and orthopaedics 23%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 407 crore (+10.2%) and operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23.9% margin versus 23.0%. B2C:B2B mix improved to 53:47 from 51:49; preventive share rose to 14% from 12% and specialised to 35% from 34%. About 10.5 million tests processed and over 200 customer touch points added in the quarter.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 174 crore, up 13.3% YoY, about 8% of consolidated revenue, broadly in line with Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin target of about 25% in roughly two years (FY28); management said it is now aspired to be achieved after ESOP cost, and Q1 is a dip versus this path.
Management retained the consolidated margin guidance; analysts had cited 150-200 bps hospital margin expansion for FY27, which management did not restate as ESOP-inclusive.
ESOP charge expected around INR 40 crore per quarter for the rest of FY27 if headcount is unchanged, falling to about INR 30 crore per quarter and then about INR 25 crore per quarter in year three.
Diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year, per the CFO; the Agilus CEO reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance.
Plan to add about 400 beds in the remaining three quarters of FY27, including about 200 beds at FMRI pending an occupancy certificate expected imminently. Q1 added about 100 beds.

Manesar radiation oncology equipment expected to be commissioned by November 2026, after which it becomes a comprehensive oncology centre; Manesar and Greater Noida expected to reach mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.
Capex: growth is expected to consume about 50% of EBITDA through brownfield expansion, excluding acquisitions; proton therapy in Gurgaon estimated at about INR 252 crore.
capex_capacity: Q1 added about 100 operational beds through brownfield expansion at Noida, Amritsar and Jalandhar; Manesar has about 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy.

Robotics: Da Vinci Xi soft-tissue robots installed at Faridabad and Fortis Escorts Heart Institute Okhla; ortho robots installed at Jalandhar and Faridabad. Board approved a proton facility at the Gurgaon flagship, capex about INR 252 crore, still being finalised.
Entered Odisha via an O&M agreement for a 300-bed greenfield hospital in Cuttack; no capital committed.
Oncology build-out: three units (Faridabad brownfield block, Amritsar and Jaipur) are starting work to become full cancer hospitals.
Company is pursuing inorganic deals in existing clusters (Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Punjab, MMR, Kolkata); no details disclosed. Gleneagles O&M discussions with IHH ongoing.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy flat at 69% as occupied beds grew 17%; management said the core base consistently runs around 70% and levers can add 2-3 percentage points.

Oncology growth slowed from about 23-24% to about 5% because a 30% discount on chemo drug MRP under ECHS/CGHS pricing is hitting Punjab, Jaipur and NCR units; management expects 10-12% growth going forward.
Doctor poaching described as ongoing but not a major concern; ESOP scheme is broad-based across zones, covering roughly 55-60% doctors and administrative staff.
Diagnostics market described as competitive; management acknowledged muted or stagnant growth in prior periods due to rebranding, and the Agilus CEO (recently joined) is reworking plans.
Gleneagles O&M fee is 3% of revenue, about INR 6 crore booked in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP charge for FY27 and the next two years, and can consolidated margin improve by 100 bps in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the charge will be higher initially and fall over about three years; it still maintained margin guidance, citing cost savings and efficiency gains from the ESOP.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% margin target pre- or post-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 25% target now aspires to be achieved after ESOP cost, expected in about two years, with levers including ramp-up of new units (from -0.4% drag to +1%), new doctor teams, lower legal costs and recovery of doubtful debt provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Manesar and Greater Noida margins below 10%, and when will they reach 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar had 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy with radiation oncology due by November; management expects both hospitals to be in the mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.

qa_highlights.question: Diagnostics growth lags industry; what are the challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: The Agilus CEO, in role about 10 days, said the company is reworking plans; B2C mix target rises to 55% and then 58%, and the company cited a rebrand and lab-network rationalisation affecting growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oncology slowdown and is it chemo-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the chemo pricing mechanism with a 30% MRP discount for ECHS and CGHS beneficiaries is the cause; oncology growth fell to about 5% from 23-24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and are acquisitions expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex is about 50% of EBITDA excluding acquisitions for the 2,000-bed expansion; inorganic deals are being pursued, expected to be in focus clusters, with no details yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are diagnostics margin and growth expectations for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO guided diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year.

risks_watch: Hospital margin dilution: Q1 at 21.5% versus 22.1%, with new units still dragging, ESOP charge of about INR 40 crore per quarter and rising doubtful-debt provisions from government and TPA payors.
Oncology pricing pressure from the chemo drug pricing mechanism in ECHS/CGHS segments; growth fell to about 5%.
Diagnostics growth lagging peers (about 10% vs industry about 15%) amid leadership change and reworking of plans.
Legal costs linked to the Delhi High Court proceedings (Gleneagles-related, per call context) continue into coming quarters.
Net debt up to INR 2,233 crore with capex plus inorganic spend; watch leverage versus 1.01x.
Manesar occupancy and oncology commissioning by November; Gleneagles O&M and IHH discussions outcome.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets but cautious on near-term margins: management repeatedly declined to give numbers on several items and acknowledged that Q1 margin is a dip and Manesar profitability is below expectation. Diagnostics commentary was more defensive, with the new CEO still reworking plans.
key_quotes: We are pretty confident that we are still on track.
Overall, in two years' time, we are quite hopeful that we will be reaching to 25%.
We are aspiring to achieve 25% EBITDA margin after running the ESOP cost.
We are completely on the path that we will be able to achieve similar levels within, say, next few quarters.

adds.what: ~100 beds added in Q1 via brownfield expansion at Noida, Amritsar and Jalandhar
~400 beds to be operationalised in remaining 3 quarters of FY27, incl. ~200 beds at FMRI pending occupancy certificate
Manesar radiation oncology equipment to convert it into comprehensive oncology centre
Proton therapy facility at Gurgaon flagship (board approved, still being finalised)

growth.why: Q1 consolidated revenue +17.5% with occupied beds +17% and ~100 beds added; ~400 more beds planned for rest of FY27 (partly backed by named units like FMRI, pending occupancy certificate), diagnostics guided to 12-13% growth, but no company-level revenue growth number and hospital margin target of ~25% is an FY28 aspiration after ESOP costs.

mgmt.note: Agilus CEO recently joined and is reworking diagnostics plans; reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance on this call, date of change not specified in brief.
